title: Subeg Singh Invokes the Gurus as the Torture Intensifies

blocks.text: Subeg Singh answers the offers by arguing that mere survival has no value when purchased through betrayal of the Guru. The Gurus themselves surrendered their sons for the Panth, so he cannot preserve his own line by abandoning the very faith that gave his household meaning.

That appeal to precedent transforms private suffering into continuity with Sikh history. What the court sees as stubbornness, the narrative presents as disciplined remembrance of how the Gurus placed truth above lineage, comfort, and worldly security.

Frustrated by argument, the nawab abandons persuasion and orders the child's torture to be intensified again. The page thus hardens the confrontation into a direct contest between imperial cruelty and inherited Sikh resolve.
